subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix target the scheduled memory producer only, or should OpenClaw change the generic `read` tool contract for directory and optional memory paths?
rationale: The source evidence proves partial fixes and a remaining directory-read failure shape, but the safe product boundary depends on whether this is a producer bug or an intentional tool-contract change.

options.title: Fix Producer After Live Repro
options.body: Reproduce the current cron/dreaming/heartbeat path, then repair the exact producer that asks for stale, wrong, or directory paths.

options.title: Broaden Read Semantics
options.body: Make the generic read tool return directory listings or optional memory context, accepting a model-facing tool-contract change with focused tests.

options.title: Split Memory Retention Work
options.body: Keep diary and corpus growth under the existing memory-core retention trackers while this issue stays focused on repeated scheduled read failures.

recommendation.title: Fix Producer After Live Repro
recommendation.body: Reproduce the current cron/dreaming/heartbeat path, then repair the exact producer that asks for stale, wrong, or directory paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses read-tool semantics, Gateway cron behavior, and memory-core ownership, and recent history points to steipete as the broad current-path router.
